title: Property-based invariant tests
description:
Write property-based tests in tests/properties.rs using proptest. Generate random registries and random inputs, then verify canon's five core invariants hold universally.

TARGET FILE: tests/properties.rs only.

=== GENERATORS ===

Registry generator (arb_registry):
- Generate 1-100 mapping entries with random input strings (ASCII printable, 1-20 chars), random canonical_id, canonical_type from fixed set (ticker/isin/lei/counterparty_id), rule_id from fixed set
- Write to a tempdir as valid registry: registry.json + one or more mapping files
- Sometimes generate duplicate input values across files (tests first-match-wins)
- Sometimes generate empty registry (zero entries)

Input generator (arb_csv_input):
- Generate CSV with 1-500 rows, header always includes the target column
- Column values drawn from: registry inputs (will resolve), random strings (won't resolve), empty strings, mix
- Sometimes include blank rows (all fields empty)
- Delimiter: randomly comma, tab, or pipe

Input generator (arb_jsonl_input):
- Generate JSONL with 1-500 lines
- Field values drawn from: registry inputs, random strings, null, missing field, nested objects/arrays, numbers, booleans
- Tests all five special reason paths

=== INVARIANTS (verified for every generated case) ===

1. COMPLETENESS: summary.total == summary.resolved + summary.unresolved
   Parse JSON output, check arithmetic identity.

2. DETERMINISM: run canon twice with identical input + registry, outputs are byte-identical.
   Run binary twice, compare stdout bytes.

3. PARTITION: every unique input value appears in exactly one of mappings[] or unresolved[], never both, never missing.
   Collect all inputs from mappings + unresolved, verify it's a partition of the unique input values.

4. TRACEABILITY: every mappings[].rule_id + mappings[].input references a real entry in the registry.
   Load the registry files, verify each mapping's input/rule_id pair exists as an entry.

5. CROSS-MODE CONSISTENCY: for CSV input, run both --emit json and --emit csv on the same input+registry. Verify:
   - Each resolved row's canonical column value matches the corresponding mappings[].canonical_id (after stripping u8: prefix)
   - Each unresolved row's canonical column is empty
   - Row count in CSV output matches input row count

=== TEST STRUCTURE ===

proptest! {
    #[test]
    fn invariant_completeness(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_determinism(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_partition(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_traceability(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_cross_mode(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_jsonl_completeness(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_jsonl_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_jsonl_partition(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_jsonl_input()) { ... }
}

=== PROPTEST CONFIG ===

Use ProptestConfig with cases=512 for CI (fast), PROPTEST_CASES env var for exhaustive local runs. Persist regressions to tests/proptest-regressions/ (tracked in git, NOT gitignored).

VERIFICATION: cargo test --test properties -- --test-threads=1
acceptance_criteria:
All tests in tests/properties.rs pass with ProptestConfig { cases: 512 }.
7 property tests: invariant_completeness (CSV), invariant_determinism (CSV), invariant_partition (CSV), invariant_traceability (CSV), invariant_cross_mode (CSV), invariant_jsonl_completeness, invariant_jsonl_partition.
Generators: arb_registry (0-100 entries, valid registry dir), arb_csv_input (1-500 rows, mixed resolve/unresolve/empty/blank), arb_jsonl_input (1-500 lines, all special reasons).
proptest-regressions/ tracked in git.

IMPORTANT: proptest-regressions/ directory MUST be tracked in git (NOT gitignored) — regression files are permanent test cases that prevent known-bad inputs from recurring. Add tests/proptest-regressions/.gitkeep.

title: canon registry default-id-scheme: persist prefix convention in registry.json
description:
Add `canon registry default-id-scheme` to persist a registry's self-authored canonical ID convention in `registry.json`.

Purpose:
- A self-authored registry usually has one canonical namespace such as `PPL`, `IC`, or `CPTY`. Storing the convention makes the registry self-describing and lets `next-id` and `mint` work without repeating `--prefix` every time.

CLI:
`canon registry default-id-scheme --registry <DIR> --prefix <PREFIX> [--zero-pad <N>] [--strict] [--bump patch|minor|major | --next-version <VER>] [--emit json|plain]`

Behavior:
- Read `registry.json` as a JSON object and set `default_id_scheme` to `{ "prefix": <PREFIX>, "zero_pad": <N> }`.
- Validate `PREFIX` as `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*$` and `zero_pad` as an integer from 1 through 20. Default width is 3.
- Preserve all existing `registry.json` fields and formatting can change only through pretty JSON serialization.
- Version update uses the same mutually exclusive `--next-version` or `--bump` rules as add-entry, defaulting to patch when the current version is bumpable.
- Increment no mapping entries. `entry_count` should remain unchanged because this is registry metadata, not a mapping addition.
- Inspect existing `canonical_id` values. By default, emit warnings for IDs that start with the prefix namespace but do not conform to the scheme. With `--strict`, refuse instead of writing.
- Write `registry.json` atomically or leave the original bytes unchanged on failure.
- Do not mutate mapping files or `_index.sqlite`.
- Do not add new witness behavior in this bead.
- Ensure `next-id` without a prefix and `mint` without `--canonical-id` or `--prefix` consume the configured scheme.

Output:
- Default `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_default_id_scheme.v0` with registry version before/after, previous scheme, new scheme, warning counts, and touched file.
- `--emit plain`: print `<PREFIX>-<zero_pad width>` style summary plus newline, for example `PPL-3`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Setting the scheme writes `default_id_scheme` to `registry.json` and bumps the registry version without changing `entry_count`.
- Unknown `registry.json` fields survive unchanged.
- Invalid prefixes, zero padding outside 1..20, and unchanged/non-bumpable versions refuse with recovery guidance.
- `--strict` refuses when existing in-namespace canonical IDs do not conform; non-strict mode writes and records warnings in the JSON receipt.
- `canon registry next-id --registry <DIR>` uses the configured scheme when no prefix is supplied.
- `canon registry mint --registry <DIR> --canonical-type <TYPE> --with-alias ...` uses the configured scheme when no canonical ID or prefix is supplied.
- JSON receipt shape is covered by a golden fixture for `canon_registry_default_id_scheme.v0`.
- The command writes only `registry.json`; mapping files and `_index.sqlite` are unchanged.
- Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.
notes:
Target files:
- src/registry/id_scheme.rs (new)
- src/registry.rs (add module/export and extend metadata helpers; there is no src/registry/mod.rs in this repo)
- src/registry/next_id.rs (fallback behavior, if not already complete)
- src/registry/mint.rs (fallback behavior, if not already complete)
- src/cli.rs (wire subcommand)
- src/lib.rs (minimal dispatch only)
- operator.json (add command contract if implemented in this bead)
- tests/registry_id_scheme.rs (new)

Implementation notes:
- This bead should land after next-id and mint to avoid parallel edits to the same modules.
- `default_id_scheme` is metadata for self-authored registries. It must not alter lookup matching semantics.
- Keep the field optional; existing registries without it must continue to load and resolve exactly as before.
close_reason: Implemented canon registry default-id-scheme as a metadata-only registry.json writer. Validates prefix and zero_pad, bumps version without changing entry_count, preserves unknown registry fields, records non-strict warnings for in-namespace out-of-scheme IDs, supports --strict refusal, leaves mappings and _index.sqlite untouched, and proves next-id/mint consume the stored scheme. Evidence: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test; target/debug/canon --describe includes default-id-scheme; br dep cycles --json returned count 0.

title: Project skeleton + core types
description:
Pre-swarm foundation. Create Cargo.toml, src/main.rs, src/lib.rs with module stubs and ALL shared types that cross module boundaries. Must compile before agents start. This is the contract 8 agents code against.

Cargo.toml: name=canon, version=0.1.0, edition=2024. [[bin]] name=canon path=src/main.rs. Deps: clap 4 (derive), csv 1, serde 1 (derive), serde_json 1, rusqlite (bundled), blake3 1. Dev-deps: tempfile 3, assert_cmd 2, predicates 3. Release profile: opt-level=z, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip=true.

src/main.rs: #![forbid(unsafe_code)], parse args via cli::Cli, call canon::run(), map exit code (0/1/2).

src/lib.rs: #![forbid(unsafe_code)], mod declarations (cli, input, registry, lookup, output, refusal, witness). pub fn run(cli: cli::Cli) -> Result<u8, Box<dyn Error>> stub returning Ok(0).

=== OUTPUT MODULE SPLIT (CRITICAL FOR PARALLELISM) ===

The output module MUST be a directory, not a flat file:
- src/output/mod.rs: pub mod json; pub mod csv;
- src/output/json.rs: stub for JSON emission (bd-2p4 agent's target)
- src/output/csv.rs: stub for CSV emission (bd-37k agent's target)

This split enables bd-2p4 and bd-37k to work in parallel without file conflicts.

=== SHARED TYPES (all pub, derives noted) ===

CRITICAL: Mapping.input and Mapping.canonical_id hold RAW byte values (no u8:/hex: prefix). Identifier encoding is applied ONLY by the JSON output module at serialization time. This keeps the in-memory types format-agnostic — CSV output reads raw values directly.

Output types:
- Outcome { Resolved, Partial, Unresolved, Refusal } — #[serde(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")] so Resolved => "RESOLVED", etc.
- Mapping { input: String, canonical_id: String, canonical_type: String, rule_id: String, confidence: String } — NOTE: input/canonical_id are RAW values. JSON output applies u8:/hex: encoding via a custom serialization wrapper, NOT via the Mapping struct's Serialize impl.
- UnresolvedEntry { input: Option<String>, reason: String } — input is RAW or None for special reasons
- RegistryMeta { id: String, version: String, source: String } — source is CLI arg verbatim
- Summary { total: usize, resolved: usize, unresolved: usize }
- CanonOutput { version: String, outcome: Outcome, registry: Option<RegistryMeta>, summary: Option<Summary>, mappings: Vec<Mapping>, unresolved: Vec<UnresolvedEntry>, refusal: Option<Refusal> }

Refusal types:
- RefusalCode enum: EIo, EEncoding, ECsvParse, EBadRegistry, EColumnNotFound, EParse, EEmptyInput, ETooLarge, EEmitFormat, EColumnExists — custom Serialize to emit "E_IO", etc.
- Refusal { code: RefusalCode, message: String, detail: serde_json::Value, next_command: Option<String> }

Cross-module types (the 8-agent contract):
- InputFormat enum { Csv, Jsonl }
- SpecialReason enum { EmptyValue, NullValue, MissingField, NonScalarValue } — Display impl yields "empty_value", etc.
- InputValues { values: HashMap<String, ()>, special: HashMap<SpecialReason, usize>, format: InputFormat, delimiter: Option<u8> }
- Registry { meta: RegistryMeta, db_path: PathBuf }
- ResolveResult { mappings: Vec<Mapping>, unresolved: Vec<UnresolvedEntry>, summary: Summary }

Module stubs created: src/cli.rs, src/input.rs, src/registry.rs, src/lookup.rs, src/output/mod.rs, src/output/json.rs, src/output/csv.rs, src/refusal.rs, src/witness.rs. Each stub includes placeholder function signatures AND a #[cfg(test)] mod tests {} block.

title: canon registry next-id: deterministic id-allocator for self-authored registries
description:
Add `canon registry next-id [PREFIX]` as a read-only helper for self-authored registries.

Purpose:
- Operators who own a registry need a deterministic way to choose the next canonical ID under a local convention such as `PPL-001`, `IC-002`, or `CPTY-00042`.
- This command does not create an entity and does not mutate registry files. It only inspects the current flat mapping entries and suggests the next available ID.

CLI:
`canon registry next-id [PREFIX] --registry <DIR> [--zero-pad <N>] [--emit plain|json]`

Behavior:
- Read `registry.json` and all flat mapping files using the same discovery exclusions and filename ordering as the normal registry loader: all root `*.json` except `registry.json` and `_build.json`; subdirectories ignored.
- Validate `PREFIX` as `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*$`.
- If `PREFIX` is omitted, read `registry.json.default_id_scheme.prefix` and `zero_pad` when present; otherwise refuse with a next-command that includes an explicit prefix.
- `--zero-pad` overrides the scheme width for this read-only suggestion. Default width is 3.
- Collect distinct `canonical_id` values, filter IDs matching exactly `<PREFIX>-<digits>`, compute the numeric max, and return max + 1 padded to the selected width.
- If no matching IDs exist, return `<PREFIX>-001` or the selected zero-padded equivalent.
- Refuse if any canonical ID starts with `<PREFIX>-` but the suffix is not all ASCII digits. This prevents silently skipping malformed IDs inside the selected namespace.
- Do not write registry files, do not update `_index.sqlite`, and do not add new witness behavior in this bead. Keep side effects read-only.

Output:
- Default `--emit plain`: print only the suggested ID plus newline, for shell composition.
- `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_next_id.v0` with `registry`, `scheme`, `current_max`, `next_id`, `entry_count_matching_prefix`, and `warnings` fields.
acceptance_criteria:
- `canon registry next-id PPL --registry <DIR>` returns `PPL-001` for a valid empty registry.
- Existing IDs are scanned across all root mapping files and the command returns max + 1 deterministically.
- Duplicate canonical IDs are counted once for max computation, while `entry_count_matching_prefix` reports distinct IDs in the namespace.
- `--zero-pad` is honored, including widths larger than 3.
- Omitted prefix uses `registry.json.default_id_scheme` when present and refuses with a concrete next-command when absent.
- Malformed in-namespace IDs such as `PPL-ABC` or `PPL-12A` cause a refusal; out-of-namespace IDs are ignored.
- JSON output matches a golden fixture for `canon_registry_next_id.v0`.
- Plain output contains only the ID and newline.
- The command has no filesystem writes except normal Beads/test fixture setup; `_index.sqlite` is not created as a side effect of next-id.
- Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.

title: canon registry mint: compose next-id + add-entry for one-shot self-authored mints
description:
Add `canon registry mint` as the one-shot self-authored entity creation workflow built from `next-id` and `add-entry` internals.

Purpose:
- Make the common workflow ergonomic: choose or provide a canonical ID, add one or more starting aliases for that ID, bump registry metadata once, validate once, and emit a receipt.
- `mint` creates durable registry knowledge only through mapping entries. It must not create an invisible allocated ID that cannot resolve later.

CLI:
`canon registry mint --registry <DIR> [--canonical-id <ID> | --prefix <PREFIX>] --canonical-type <TYPE> --with-alias <FILE=INPUT:RULE_ID>... [--bump patch|minor|major | --next-version <VER>] [--no-lint] [--emit json|plain]`

Behavior:
- Require at least one `--with-alias`. Refuse no-alias mints; reserving unused IDs would require a separate documented allocation sidecar and is out of scope for this bead.
- If `--canonical-id` is omitted, call the internal next-id allocator using `--prefix` or `registry.json.default_id_scheme`. `--prefix` overrides the configured default for this operation.
- Parse `--with-alias` by splitting once at `=` and then splitting the right side at the last `:`. This lets inputs contain colons while keeping `rule_id` required and non-empty.
- Each alias file must satisfy the same validation as `add-entry`: existing root-level `.json`, no path traversal, not `registry.json` or `_build.json`.
- Validate all aliases and all target files before writing anything. Duplicate inputs against existing registry entries or within the mint request must refuse.
- Apply one registry version change for the entire mint. Do not call an add-entry path that bumps once per alias.
- Version update uses the same mutually exclusive `--next-version` or `--bump` rules as add-entry, defaulting to patch when the current version is bumpable.
- Increment `entry_count` by the number of alias entries actually added and preserve all other `registry.json` fields.
- If lint is enabled, validate the final proposed registry once and abort on lint errors; warnings/info appear in the receipt.
- Commit all touched alias files plus `registry.json` atomically as a unit, or restore byte-for-byte originals on failure.
- Do not directly mutate `_index.sqlite`; let the normal loader rebuild from mapping files and the bumped version.
- Do not add new witness behavior in this bead.

Output:
- Default `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_mint.v0` with `canonical_id`, `canonical_type`, alias entries added, registry version before/after, touched files, lint summary, and warnings.
- `--emit plain`: print only the minted canonical ID plus newline.

title: Input parsing (CSV + JSONL)
description:
Parse both CSV and JSONL input formats in src/input.rs. Return a unified InputValues structure (unique values + special-case classifications) consumed by the lookup engine.

CSV parsing:
- csv crate (streaming). Header required, UTF-8 BOM stripped.
- Delimiter auto-detected (same algorithm as rvl: sniff first 8KB for comma/tab/pipe/semicolon frequency).
- --column specifies column name. Must exist (else E_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND).
- Skip blank records (all fields empty after ASCII-trim).
- ASCII-trim values before collection. Empty after trim => classify as empty_value (no lookup).

JSONL parsing:
- One JSON object per line. --column specifies field name.
- Missing field => classify as missing_field.
- null value => classify as null_value (not string-coerced to "null").
- Object/array value => classify as non_scalar_value.
- Numbers/booleans coerced to JSON string representation (42 => "42").
- String values ASCII-trimmed. Empty after trim => classify as empty_value.
- Stdin support (- for JSONL only; CSV requires seekable input).

Format detection:
- .csv and .tsv => CSV parser.
- .jsonl and .ndjson => JSONL parser.
- Unrecognized or missing extension => E_PARSE refusal.

=== I/O BUDGET ENFORCEMENT ===

--max-bytes (Option<u64>): For regular files, check file size BEFORE reading (stat the file, compare, refuse E_TOO_LARGE if over). For stdin (JSONL only), count bytes during streaming and refuse E_TOO_LARGE as soon as the limit is exceeded.

--max-rows (Option<usize>): Count raw data rows during streaming (including duplicates, excluding header for CSV and excluding blank records). Refuse E_TOO_LARGE if the count exceeds the limit. This is an I/O budget, not a cardinality limit.

Both checks use refusal code E_TOO_LARGE with detail indicating which limit was hit and what the actual value was.

=== EMPTY INPUT CHECK ===

After parsing completes, if values is empty AND special is empty, refuse with E_EMPTY_INPUT. This covers: header-only CSV, empty JSONL file, CSV where all rows are blank records. This check MUST happen here (not in run()) so the zero-values-zero-specials case never reaches the lookup engine.

=== ENCODING ERRORS ===

Non-UTF-8 files that fail decoding => refuse E_ENCODING (not E_CSV_PARSE). Malformed-but-UTF-8 CSV => E_CSV_PARSE. The distinction matters for the next_command recovery guidance.

Output: InputValues struct containing:
- values: HashMap<String, ()> of unique non-special input values
- special: HashMap<SpecialReason, usize> counts of empty_value/null_value/missing_field/non_scalar_value
- format: InputFormat enum (Csv/Jsonl) for downstream emit-mode validation
- delimiter: Option<u8> — the detected CSV delimiter (Some for CSV, None for JSONL). Required by the CSV output module to preserve delimiter in --emit csv mode.

title: Registry loading + SQLite index
description:
Implement registry loading and SQLite index building in src/registry.rs.

Loading:
- Read registry.json from --registry path. Parse into RegistryMeta (id, version, description, updated, entry_count).
- Discover mapping files: all *.json in directory except registry.json. Flat directory only (subdirs ignored). Non-JSON files ignored.
- Validate each mapping file: must be a JSON array of objects, each with { input, canonical_id, canonical_type, rule_id }. Malformed => return E_BAD_REGISTRY.
- Log stderr warning if entry_count in registry.json differs from actual discovered entry count.

SQLite index:
- Derived index stored as _index.sqlite inside the registry directory.
- Schema: entries(input TEXT, canonical_id TEXT, canonical_type TEXT, rule_id TEXT, source_file TEXT, entry_order INTEGER).
- Entries ordered by (source_file ASC, entry_order ASC) for first-match-wins precedence.
- Staleness check: compare registry.json version string + max file mtime of *.json files against metadata table in SQLite.
- Auto-rebuild when stale. Log rebuild to stderr.
- If registry dir is not writable (can't create _index.sqlite), fall back to in-memory SQLite (build once per run, log warning).

Return type: Registry { meta: RegistryMeta, db_path: PathBuf } (the db_path points to _index.sqlite; lookup module opens it).

Error cases:
- Missing registry dir => E_IO
- Missing registry.json => E_BAD_REGISTRY
- Malformed mapping files => E_BAD_REGISTRY
- Empty registry (valid format, zero entries) => load succeeds (zero entries is valid; outcome will be UNRESOLVED)

title: canon strategy — frozen script resolution by schema shape + skill hash
description:
New resolution mode for canon: resolve a schema shape + skill hash to a frozen champion script.

## Concept

Canon resolves messy inputs to canonical outputs using versioned registries. Canon strategy extends this to resolve schema shapes to frozen scripts:

- Input: schema fingerprint (from profile stats) + skill hash (from the skill file that authored the script)
- Output: a frozen Python/shell script that passed verify + assess + airlock
- Registry: versioned, grows across clients, compounds per PRC-COMPOUND-006

## Resolution tiers

Same semantics as entity canon:
- EXACT: identical columns, types, cardinalities → run frozen champion
- COMPATIBLE: same columns, different cardinalities → run frozen champion (script still works)
- PARTIAL: overlapping columns, some missing → ESCALATE (LLM rewrites)
- UNRESOLVED: different domain → LLM authors new script, gates it, registers on success

## Registration flow

1. profile stats produces schema fingerprint
2. Skill file is hashed (the skill that authored the script is part of the lookup key)
3. canon strategy resolve checks registry for (schema shape, skill hash) tuple
4. If UNRESOLVED: LLM writes script → verify PASS → assess PROCEED → canon strategy register
5. If RESOLVED: frozen script runs directly, no LLM, deterministic output

## Why skill hash matters

The same schema could produce different scripts depending on which skill authored it. A procurement skill and a compliance skill both operating on the same CSV shape should resolve to different champion scripts. Hashing the skill into the lookup key prevents cross-skill contamination.

## Why this is canon, not a new primitive

- Registry is the moat (same as entity canon)
- Versioning is built in (canon already versions registries)
- Resolution semantics are identical (exact/compatible/partial/unresolved)
- Compounds across clients (PRC-COMPOUND-006)
- Dual-copy model applies (client gets output, CMD+RVL retains registry)

## Origin

Observed during procurement spine skill testing: four runs on the same data produced four different grand totals ($83K, $94K, $83K, different). All within sanity bounds, all using the same median fallback. The variation comes from the LLM writing slightly different Python each time. Canon strategy would freeze the first passing script and reuse it — same shape, same script, same numbers, every time.

title: OpenFIGI provider for registry materializer
description:
## Summary

Implement the OpenFIGI provider for `canon registry build`. This is the first real provider — it queries the OpenFIGI API (https://www.openfigi.com/api) and materializes FIGI mappings into a standard canon registry.

## What is OpenFIGI

The Financial Instrument Global Identifier (FIGI) is an open standard published by the Object Management Group (OMG). OpenFIGI is Bloomberg's free API that maps between FIGIs and other identifier types (CUSIP, ISIN, SEDOL, ticker, composite FIGI). It is the canonical cross-reference for financial instrument identifiers.

**API details:**
- Endpoint: `https://api.openfigi.com/v3/mapping`
- Method: POST with JSON array of mapping jobs
- Rate limits: 25 requests/minute (free, no API key), 250 requests/minute (with free API key)
- Batch size: up to 100 identifiers per request
- No authentication required for basic use; optional API key via `X-OPENFIGI-APIKEY` header for higher rate limits

## Design

### Provider implementation

```rust
pub struct OpenFigiProvider {
    api_key: Option<String>,   // optional, from --provider-config or env OPENFIGI_API_KEY
    base_url: String,          // default: https://api.openfigi.com/v3/mapping
    id_type: String,           // "ID_CUSIP", "ID_ISIN", "ID_SEDOL", etc.
}
```

### API request format

```json
[
  {"idType": "ID_CUSIP", "idValue": "037833100"},
  {"idType": "ID_CUSIP", "idValue": "594918104"},
  {"idType": "ID_CUSIP", "idValue": "17275R102"}
]
```

### API response format

Each identifier returns zero or more FIGI records:

```json
[
  {"data": [{"figi": "BBG000B9XRY4", "name": "APPLE INC", "ticker": "AAPL", "exchCode": "US", "compositeFIGI": "BBG000B9XRY4", "securityType": "Common Stock"}]},
  {"data": [{"figi": "BBG000BPH459", "name": "MICROSOFT CORP", "ticker": "MSFT", ...}]},
  {"data": [{"figi": "BBG00QFYFL90", "name": "COINBASE GLOBAL INC", "ticker": "COIN", ...}]}
]
```

### Mapping extraction

From each OpenFIGI response, extract multiple mapping types into separate registry files:

| Registry file | Mapping | Example |
|--------------|---------|---------|
| cusip-to-figi.json | CUSIP → composite FIGI | 037833100 → BBG000B9XRY4 |
| cusip-to-ticker.json | CUSIP → ticker | 037833100 → AAPL |
| cusip-to-name.json | CUSIP → security name | 037833100 → APPLE INC |

Each mapping entry uses the standard canon format:
```json
{"input": "037833100", "canonical_id": "BBG000B9XRY4", "canonical_type": "composite_figi", "rule_id": "OPENFIGI_CUSIP_TO_FIGI"}
```

### Multi-result handling

OpenFIGI can return multiple FIGIs for a single CUSIP (different share classes, exchanges, security types). The provider must handle this:

- **composite_figi** is usually unique per identifier — prefer this as the primary mapping
- If multiple results, take the one matching the most common security type for the id type (e.g., "Common Stock" for equity CUSIPs)
- Record all results in _build.json for transparency, but the registry file gets the best single match
- If no clear winner, mark as ambiguous in _build.json and exclude from registry (conservative — don't guess)

### CLI integration

```bash
# Basic: materialize CUSIPs from a positions file
canon registry build --source openfigi \
  --seed positions.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ \
  --version "2026.03.05"

# With API key for higher rate limits
OPENFIGI_API_KEY=xxx canon registry build --source openfigi \
  --seed positions.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ \
  --version "2026.03.05"

# ISINs instead of CUSIPs
canon registry build --source openfigi \
  --seed positions.csv --seed-column isin \
  --provider-config id_type=ID_ISIN \
  --output registries/openfigi-isin/ \
  --version "2026.03.05"
```

### Rate limiting

- Free tier: 25 req/min, 100 IDs per request = 2,500 IDs/minute
- With API key: 250 req/min = 25,000 IDs/minute
- For a typical 5,000-CUSIP seed list: ~2 minutes (free) or ~12 seconds (with key)
- Provider reports rate limit status via the trait's rate_limit() method
- Framework handles backoff and retry on 429 responses

## Acceptance criteria

- OpenFIGI provider implements the RegistryProvider trait from bd-2zo
- Queries the real OpenFIGI API (integration tests can use a mock HTTP server)
- Respects rate limits (25/min free, 250/min with key)
- Batches identifiers (100 per request)
- Handles multi-result responses conservatively (composite FIGI preferred, ambiguous excluded)
- Supports CUSIP, ISIN, and SEDOL as seed id types via --provider-config
- Optional API key via env var or --provider-config
- Produced registry is a valid, standard canon registry that resolves normally
- _build.json includes: API calls made, identifiers submitted, resolved, failed, ambiguous, wall clock time
- Unit tests: mock HTTP responses for success, partial failure, rate limit, ambiguous multi-result
- Integration test: end-to-end with mock server → registry → canon resolution
close_reason: Added OpenFIGI provider support with provider-config plumbing, conservative multi-result handling, retry-aware HTTP fetches, provenance diagnostics, and end-to-end mock-server coverage

title: Registry diff and changelog (canon registry diff)
description:
## Summary

Add `canon registry diff` to compare two registry versions and report what changed. Essential operational tooling for materialized registries — when you re-materialize from OpenFIGI weekly, you need to know what changed before you start resolving against the new version.

## Motivation

Materialized registries are snapshots. When you re-materialize, identifiers get added (new instruments issued), removed (instruments delisted), or changed (corporate actions — ticker changes, mergers). Without diff, you are resolving against a new registry version blind. With diff, you know exactly what shifted and can assess impact before updating your pipeline.

This also feeds the spine: `canon registry diff` output can be piped to `rvl` for materiality analysis — "of the 47 mappings that changed, which ones affect positions I actually hold?"

## Design

### Subcommand

```bash
canon registry diff \
  --old registries/openfigi-cusip-v2026.02/ \
  --new registries/openfigi-cusip-v2026.03/ \
  [--emit json|summary]
```

### Output (JSON)

```json
{
  "version": "canon_registry_diff.v0",
  "old": { "id": "openfigi-cusip", "version": "2026.02.28" },
  "new": { "id": "openfigi-cusip", "version": "2026.03.05" },
  "summary": {
    "total_old": 4183,
    "total_new": 4210,
    "added": 34,
    "removed": 7,
    "changed": 12,
    "unchanged": 4157
  },
  "added": [
    { "input": "92936U101", "canonical_id": "BBG01ABCDEF0", "canonical_type": "composite_figi", "rule_id": "OPENFIGI_CUSIP_TO_FIGI" }
  ],
  "removed": [
    { "input": "78462F103", "canonical_id": "BBG000BVG4K0", "canonical_type": "composite_figi", "reason": "not_in_new_registry" }
  ],
  "changed": [
    {
      "input": "931142103",
      "old": { "canonical_id": "BBG000BJ2GK0", "canonical_type": "composite_figi" },
      "new": { "canonical_id": "BBG00XXXXXXX", "canonical_type": "composite_figi" },
      "change_type": "figi_change"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Summary mode

```bash
$ canon registry diff --old v2026.02/ --new v2026.03/ --emit summary
openfigi-cusip: 2026.02.28 → 2026.03.05
  +34 added, -7 removed, ~12 changed, =4157 unchanged
  Notable: 3 ticker changes (corporate actions), 7 delistings
```

### Composability with the spine

```bash
# What changed in the registry?
canon registry diff --old v2026.02/ --new v2026.03/ > evidence/registry-diff.json

# Which changes affect my positions?
# (extract changed input IDs, filter positions file, run rvl)
canon registry diff --old v2026.02/ --new v2026.03/ \
  | jq -r '.changed[].input' > /tmp/changed-cusips.txt

# Seal the evidence
pack seal evidence/ --note "Registry update 2026.02 → 2026.03"
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `canon registry diff --old <dir> --new <dir>` compares two registry versions
- Reports added, removed, changed, unchanged counts
- JSON output includes full detail for each category
- Summary mode (--emit summary) gives human-readable one-liner
- Both registries must have the same id (refuse if comparing apples to oranges)
- Handles registries with different mapping file sets (old has cusip-to-figi.json only, new adds cusip-to-ticker.json)
- Deterministic output: same two registries = same diff, always
- Tests: known registries with specific additions, removals, and changes

title: Lookup engine (exact match)
description:
Implement the lookup engine in src/lookup.rs.

Takes InputValues (from input module) and Registry (from registry module), resolves each unique value against the SQLite index, returns ResolveResult.

Process:
1. Open SQLite connection to Registry.db_path.
2. For each value in InputValues.values: query entries table for exact byte match on input column. First match wins (ORDER BY source_file ASC, entry_order ASC LIMIT 1).
3. If match found: create Mapping { input (raw), canonical_id, canonical_type, rule_id, confidence: "deterministic" }.
4. If no match: create UnresolvedEntry { input: Some(raw_value), reason: "no matching rule" }.
5. For each SpecialReason in InputValues.special (where count > 0): create UnresolvedEntry { input: None, reason: special_reason.to_string() }. At most one entry per distinct reason regardless of count.
6. Build Summary: total = mappings.len() + unresolved.len(), resolved = mappings.len(), unresolved_count = unresolved.len(). Invariant: total == resolved + unresolved_count.
7. Determine outcome (not stored in ResolveResult — derived by caller from summary counts).

Performance: batch queries where possible. For large InputValues, consider prepared statement reuse.
acceptance_criteria: TARGET FILE: src/lookup.rs only. Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests. Test: exact match lookup, no-match unresolved, special reason entries (one per distinct reason), summary invariant (total == resolved + unresolved), first-match-wins precedence. VERIFICATION: cargo test -- lookup

title: JSON output emission (canon.v0 schema)
description:
Implement JSON output emission in src/output/json.rs.

TARGET FILE: src/output/json.rs ONLY. Do not touch src/output/csv.rs or src/output/mod.rs.

Takes a ResolveResult + RegistryMeta, builds a CanonOutput, and serializes to JSON.

IMPORTANT: Mapping.input and Mapping.canonical_id in the ResolveResult hold RAW values. This module MUST apply identifier encoding before JSON serialization:
- u8:<value> if the value is valid UTF-8 with no ASCII control bytes (0x00-0x1F, 0x7F)
- hex:<lowercase-hex-bytes> otherwise

UnresolvedEntry.input: same encoding rules. If None (special reasons), serialize as JSON null.

Outcome derivation:
- summary.resolved > 0 && summary.unresolved == 0 => RESOLVED
- summary.resolved > 0 && summary.unresolved > 0 => PARTIAL
- summary.resolved == 0 && summary.unresolved > 0 => UNRESOLVED

For REFUSAL outcomes: use Refusal::to_canon_output() from the refusal module. This module only handles RESOLVED/PARTIAL/UNRESOLVED.

Output is a single JSON object on stdout (compact, no trailing newline). The same format is used for --map-out sidecar files (CSV mode's JSON artifact).

title: Witness protocol
description:
Implement the witness protocol in src/witness.rs. ~100-150 LOC.

Purpose: append an immutable ledger record for every canon run, enabling audit trail and reproducibility verification.

Hashing:
- input_hash: BLAKE3 hash of the input file bytes (read the file once, hash all bytes).
- output_hash: BLAKE3 hash of the output bytes. JSON mode: hash the entire JSON string. CSV mode: hash the CSV bytes incrementally as they stream through stdout (wrap the stdout writer in a BLAKE3 hashing tee).

Ledger record (one JSON line appended to .canon-witness.jsonl):
{
  "tool": "canon",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-25T12:34:56.789Z",
  "input_path": "tape.csv",
  "input_hash": "blake3:abc123...",
  "output_hash": "blake3:def456...",
  "registry_id": "cusip-isin",
  "registry_version": "3.2.1",
  "outcome": "PARTIAL",
  "summary": { "total": 100, "resolved": 95, "unresolved": 5 }
}

Ledger location: .canon-witness.jsonl in the current working directory.

Error handling: witness failures NEVER block the main pipeline. If the ledger file can't be opened/written, log a warning to stderr and continue. The tool's primary output (JSON or CSV) is never affected by witness failure.

--no-witness: if set, skip the entire witness step (no hashing, no file write).

title: Registry materializer framework (canon registry build)
description:
## Summary

Add a `canon registry build` subcommand that materializes external data sources into standard canon registry directories. This is the framework — provider-specific implementations (OpenFIGI, etc.) are separate beads.

## Motivation

Canon resolves identifiers against static, versioned, local registries. This is the right design — determinism, reproducibility, offline use, diffability. But building those registries by hand is tedious and error-prone. Industry-standard identifier databases (OpenFIGI, GLEIF/LEI, EDGAR CIK) already exist as public APIs. The materializer bridges the gap: query the API once, snapshot the results as a versioned canon registry, then resolve against the snapshot thousands of times with full determinism.

The key principle: **canon never calls an API at resolution time.** The materializer is a separate step that produces a registry. Canon consumes it like any other registry. Same input + same registry version = same output. Always.

## Design

### Subcommand

```bash
canon registry build \
  --source openfigi \
  --seed positions.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ \
  --version "2026.03.05"
```

### Seed list

The materializer needs to know which identifiers to look up. A seed file (CSV or JSONL) provides the input population. The --seed and --seed-column flags extract unique identifiers from the seed file — same dedup logic canon already uses for resolution. This means the registry is scoped to what you actually need, not the entire universe.

### Provider trait

```rust
pub trait RegistryProvider {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn fetch(&self, identifiers: &[&str], config: &ProviderConfig) -> Result<Vec<MappingEntry>>;
    fn id_types(&self) -> &[&str]; // e.g., ["cusip", "isin", "ticker", "sedol"]
    fn rate_limit(&self) -> Option<RateLimit>;
}
```

Each provider implements fetch, which takes a batch of identifiers and returns mapping entries. The framework handles: batching (respecting provider rate limits), dedup, progress reporting, error handling (partial failures → report which identifiers failed), and writing the output registry directory.

### Output

Standard canon registry directory:

```
registries/openfigi-cusip/
├── registry.json                # { id, version, source: "openfigi", materialized_at, seed_count, resolved_count }
├── cusip-to-figi.json           # Primary mappings
├── cusip-to-ticker.json         # Secondary mappings (if provider returns them)
└── _build.json                  # Build metadata: seed file hash, provider version, API calls made, failures
```

registry.json includes standard fields (id, version) plus materializer-specific metadata: source (provider name), materialized_at (ISO timestamp), seed_count (unique identifiers submitted), resolved_count (identifiers that got at least one mapping).

_build.json is build provenance — not used by canon during resolution, but useful for debugging and auditing. Includes: seed file content hash, provider name and config, number of API calls, identifiers that failed to resolve, wall clock time.

### Incremental builds

```bash
# First build: full materialization
canon registry build --source openfigi --seed tape.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ --version "2026.03.05"

# Incremental: only query identifiers not already in the registry
canon registry build --source openfigi --seed tape-updated.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ --version "2026.03.06" --incremental
```

--incremental reads the existing registry, diffs against the seed list, and only queries identifiers that are new. Existing mappings carry forward. Version bumps.

## Key files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| src/registry/build.rs | Subcommand entry point, orchestration |
| src/registry/provider.rs | Provider trait definition |
| src/registry/seed.rs | Seed list extraction (reuse input parsing) |
| src/registry/writer.rs | Registry directory writer (registry.json + mapping files) |

## Acceptance criteria

- `canon registry build --source <name> --seed <file> --seed-column <col> --output <dir> --version <ver>` produces a valid canon registry directory
- The produced registry passes canon resolution with no changes — it is a standard registry
- Provider trait is generic — adding a new provider means implementing one trait
- --incremental correctly diffs and only fetches new identifiers
- _build.json records full provenance
- Seed dedup uses the same logic as canon's input dedup
- Rate limiting is provider-configurable and respected
- Partial API failures produce warnings + the registry contains whatever succeeded
- Tests: mock provider that returns canned results, verify output registry structure
close_reason: Added canon registry build framework with mock provider, incremental materialization, provenance output, and end-to-end coverage

title: CSV output emission (--emit csv)
description:
Implement CSV output mode (--emit csv) in src/output/csv.rs.

TARGET FILE: src/output/csv.rs ONLY. Do not touch src/output/json.rs or src/output/mod.rs.

This module does ONE job: re-read the original CSV and append a canonical column using a pre-resolved map. It does NOT parse input values or resolve lookups — those are done by the input and lookup modules before this is called.

Pre-condition: run() has already validated that input format is CSV (not JSONL). This module can assume CSV input.

Input: original CSV file path, resolve_map: HashMap<String, Option<String>> mapping raw input values to canonical IDs (None for unresolved), column name, canonical column name, detected delimiter (from InputValues.delimiter), and a writer (&mut impl Write) for output.

IMPORTANT: The emit function takes a generic writer, NOT stdout directly. run() wraps stdout in a BLAKE3 hashing tee for witness protocol, then passes that writer to this module. This module writes CSV bytes to whatever writer it receives.

Behavior:
- Re-read original CSV row by row.
- Append header with canonical column name (default: <COLUMN>__canon, overridable via --canon-column).
- Pre-check: if canonical column name already in header => E_COLUMN_EXISTS refusal.
- For each data row: look up the column value in resolve_map. If Some(id), append raw canonical_id (no u8: prefix). If None, append empty string.
- Blank records: passed through with empty canonical column.
- Preserve original delimiter and quoting.
- Write to the provided writer (NOT directly to stdout).

Note: --map-out sidecar JSON is handled by run() calling the json output module, NOT by this module.

Exit codes: 0 (all resolved), 1 (partial/unresolved), 2 (refusal — no CSV written, refusal JSON to stderr).

UNIT TESTS: Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests in src/output/csv.rs. Test:
- Column appended correctly with right name
- Custom --canon-column name
- Unresolved rows get empty canonical column
- Blank rows passed through
- Delimiter preserved (comma, tab, pipe)
- Writes to a Vec<u8> writer (not stdout) in tests

VERIFICATION: cargo test -- output::csv
acceptance_criteria:
Appends canonical column as last column in header + every data row.
Default column name: <COLUMN>__canon. --canon-column overrides.
Resolved rows: raw canonical_id (no u8: prefix). Unresolved: empty string.
Blank records passed through with empty canonical column.
Delimiter and quoting match input file's detected format (uses InputValues.delimiter).
Receives pre-resolved HashMap, does NOT call lookup engine directly.
Emit function signature: pub fn emit(writer: &mut impl Write, ...) — takes a generic writer, NOT stdout directly.
Refusal E_COLUMN_EXISTS: canonical column name already exists in input header.
Refusal (exit 2): no CSV written, refusal JSON to stderr (handled by caller).
PARTIAL (exit 1): CSV fully written, unresolved rows visible not dropped.
NOTE: E_EMIT_FORMAT check is done by run() BEFORE calling this module. This module can assume input is CSV.
NOTE: --map-out sidecar JSON is handled by run(), NOT by this module.

title: canon registry add-entry: atomic single-alias-entry write + semver bump + lint
description:
Add `canon registry add-entry` as the safe single-alias writer for self-authored registries.

Purpose:
- Replace hand-editing mapping JSON with a deterministic write path that validates one new alias, bumps registry metadata, and leaves the registry in a state the normal exact lookup path can consume.
- This is registry maintenance, not a resolution workbench: no matching, no suggestions, no fuzzy behavior.

CLI:
`canon registry add-entry --registry <DIR> --alias-file <FILE> --canonical-id <ID> --input <INPUT> --rule-id <RULE> [--canonical-type <TYPE>] [--bump patch|minor|major | --next-version <VER>] [--no-lint] [--emit json|plain]`

Behavior:
- `--alias-file` must be an existing root-level mapping file name ending in `.json`; reject paths, subdirectories, `registry.json`, and `_build.json`.
- Parse all root mapping files using the existing flat registry rules before planning the write.
- Refuse if `--input` is empty after ASCII trim or is not already in trimmed form. The value written should be exactly what future lookup receives after input trim.
- Refuse if any existing mapping entry anywhere in the registry already has the same `input`, regardless of `rule_id`. First-match-wins lookup makes duplicate inputs unsafe for this writer.
- `--canonical-type` is required for a new canonical ID. If omitted for an existing canonical ID, infer it only when all existing entries for that canonical ID use exactly one canonical_type; otherwise refuse.
- If `registry.json.default_id_scheme` exists, validate `--canonical-id` against that scheme unless the command is later extended with an explicit override flag. Do not silently write out-of-scheme IDs for self-authored registries.
- Version update: accept either `--next-version <VER>` or `--bump patch|minor|major`, but not both. Default is `--bump patch`. If the current version cannot be parsed as numeric `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, refuse and require `--next-version`.
- Increment `entry_count` by one and preserve all other `registry.json` fields, including unknown metadata.
- Validate proposed output before commit. If `--no-lint` is not set, run the standard lint check and abort on lint errors; warnings/info are reported in the JSON receipt but do not block.
- Write mapping file and `registry.json` using temp-file-then-rename or an equivalent restore-on-failure sequence. A failed validation, lint error, or write error must leave the original files byte-for-byte intact.
- Do not directly mutate `_index.sqlite`; the version change should cause normal registry loading to rebuild the derived index.
- Do not add new witness behavior in this bead. Keep registry command side effects limited to the documented registry file writes.

Output:
- Default `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_add_entry.v0` with registry before/after, alias entry, touched files, lint summary, and warnings.
- `--emit plain`: emit a concise one-line success summary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Successful add-entry appends exactly one mapping object to the chosen alias file and updates `registry.json.version` and `entry_count`.
- Duplicate `input` anywhere in the registry refuses before writing and leaves all files unchanged.
- Missing `--canonical-type` is accepted only when it can be inferred unambiguously from existing entries for the canonical ID.
- Patch/minor/major bumps work for numeric three-part versions; non-bumpable versions require `--next-version`.
- `registry.json` unknown fields survive the write unchanged.
- Alias-file validation rejects path traversal, subdirectories, missing files, `registry.json`, and `_build.json`.
- Lint errors abort the write and leave all files byte-for-byte unchanged; lint warnings/info appear in the receipt.
- JSON receipt shape is covered by a golden fixture for `canon_registry_add_entry.v0`.
- A round-trip test proves a subsequent normal `canon <INPUT> --registry ...` resolves the newly added alias.
- Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.

Target files:
- src/registry/add_entry.rs (new)
- src/registry.rs (add module/export only; there is no src/registry/mod.rs in this repo)
- src/cli.rs (wire subcommand and emit/version options)

Implementation notes:

- Treat lint as data: `registry_lint::lint(..., Standard)` returns a report even with findings; only severity `error` should block by default.
- Preserve the exact-match lookup contract. This command only authors exact aliases.
